before.name: Brightly
before.description: Asset management ex-Dude Solutions, now Siemens-owned

paragraphs: Brightly sells software to track and manage the entire asset lifecycle for facilities, equipment and infrastructure. After being acquired by Siemens in 2022, the business now goes to market as Siemens.

Asset Essentials, the maintenance product, combines work order management, data and analytics, and automated preventive maintenance workflows. An AI-powered Maintenance Copilot automates routine work and surfaces instructions, summaries and safety information. Other products handle full asset lifecycle prediction modeling and capital planning. There is facility scheduling and event management software as well. Utilities are covered by cloud-based energy management software. For government infrastructure, the pitch is managing a complex network of assets in one centralized register. Field work is scheduled and allocated with native GIS capabilities.

The company describes more than 25 years supporting clients across industries in keeping critical assets and infrastructure running. It says 11,000+ organizations use the software to manage asset lifecycles. Case studies on the site include Loyola University New Orleans.

before.name: Forward Thinking Systems
before.description: IntelliHub telematics, FleetCam video, and routing for commercial and government fleets

paragraphs: Forward Thinking Systems sells fleet management technology that puts vehicle tracking, cameras, compliance, routing, driver coaching and asset management on one platform. The product itself is a browser-based console for an entire fleet.

Vehicle and driver data arrives in real time, including location, speed, ignition status and hours-of-service duty status. More than sixty built-in reports break that data down by fleet, vehicle and driver. The camera product saves footage automatically when it detects behavior such as distracted driving, hard braking or texting. A driver-facing app lets drivers watch their own scorecard, review those events, and dispute the ones they consider inaccurate. Routing is handled by a separate optimization tool for building efficient multi-stop routes.

Government and public sector fleets are one of the segments the company addresses. For those buyers it points to real-time GPS built for emergency operations. Asset tracking extends past vehicles to trailers, heavy equipment and containers. The software also integrates with fuel card providers named on the site.

before.name: Limble
before.description: Cloud CMMS for municipal facilities, water plants and public works

paragraphs: Limble sells a computerized maintenance management system for the teams that keep equipment and facilities running. The pitch is simpler work orders, assets that keep running and more productivity across every site. The company says it is rated number one by more than 50,000 maintenance professionals.

A work order can start from a dashboard, an asset record or a vendor, with details and photos added from a phone. Anyone in the organization can submit a request by scanning a QR code or visiting a URL, with no account required. Preventive maintenance is scheduled automatically on time, usage or condition. Parts inventory triggers push and email alerts when stock runs low. The mobile app keeps working without a signal and syncs once the device reconnects. Listed integrations include SAP S/4HANA, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and QuickBooks Online.

Public sector users shown include a city water treatment plant in Lompoc. The company says a team at the City of Albuquerque was confidently using the mobile app after one day of training. It reports a 4.8 out of 5 rating on G2 and Capterra from well over 1,400 combined verified reviews. It also says customers typically see value in about three weeks.

paragraphs: E.J. Ward sells automated fuel management systems to fleet operators. One platform covers fuel access, real-time monitoring, tank management, telematics, EV charging and reporting.

Access to the pump is controlled and every transaction accounted for, with reports meant to reveal anomalies. Storage tanks are watched from the same software that runs the fuel islands. paragraphs: EdgeAI provides tools and software for pipeline inspection, data analysis and repair. Its Pipe Dream robot is sold as portable, reliable technology for water and wastewater inspection at a fraction of the cost.

The crawler is designed for pipelines from 6 inches to 48 inches and larger, using optional tractor-lift or tractor-float attachments. It is light enough to be carried into tight easements or remote areas where larger systems cannot reach. The system offers live video streaming and recordings optimized up to 4K. Built-in LTE and 5G connectivity handles data upload from field sites. Customers can code the data themselves, have EdgeAI code it for them, or choose no coding depending on project needs.

The subscription model includes constant software and hardware updates. Texas BuyBoard is listed as an alternative purchasing route. notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "Baseline - Driving change by connecting communities" baseline.io is live and is the same company as 'Baseline Telematics'. I confirmed the name link independently rather than assuming it from the word 'Baseline': the PWX 2025 (APWA Public Works Expo) exhibitor listing for 'Baseline Telematics' gives its website as https://baseline.io and describes it as 'Our public sector solutions empower municipal governments to deliver better outcomes by providing the essential technology and support they need.' Corroborating: the company is Baseline Telematics Inc. of Laval, Quebec (its Facebook page is 'Baseline Telematics | Laval QC' at facebook.com/baseline.io) and its Citycare app ships under the Android package id io.baseline.citycare. Match to description: its flagship Copilot product uses smartphone telematics via the Citycare app so municipalities can track real-time route progression on a map, and the site lists 'Dispatch & Fleet Ops' with 'real-time tracking, scheduling, and analytics', plus Snowman (snow/plow ops), Airside and Resident. Caveat: the description 'Fleet telematics and GPS software' is narrower than reality - this is municipal public-works operations software with telematics inside it - but the company identity is correct and it does sell to state and local government.

paragraphs: Baseline Telematics sells software to governments, saying its public sector solutions empower municipal governments to deliver better outcomes to Canadians and Americans. The site names platforms called Resident, Citycare, Snowman, and Opera, offered to municipalities, elected officials, and public sector agencies.

Snowman covers winter road maintenance, which the site calls highly complex, expensive and risky. The company says the product gives managers real-time situational awareness during snow operations. A dispatch and fleet line offers real-time tracking, scheduling, and analytics to service companies. Another line develops usage based insurance programs with insurers and reinsurers. A further line coordinates communications and workload assignment between air traffic controllers and ground crews at Canadian airports.

The company calls itself a diversified Software-as-a-Service technology company. It ties the snow product to compliance with Ontario's Minimum Road Maintenance Standards. It also says it moved its backend to a serverless cloud function platform within 18 months.

before.name: InfraHub
before.description: Infrastructure management software platform - exhibited at PWX 2026

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "Better Data. Better Decisions. Better Roads" Fetched https://www.infrahub.ai. The page is branded InfraHub ('© 2024 InfraHub. All rights reserved', [address removed]) and the quoted tagline sits above a 'Comprehensive platform for next-generation road management'. Offerings are Pavement Survey (AI road-condition assessment to the ASTM D6433 standard), Asset Inventories (AI image recognition of roadside assets), and a Road Management Platform for maintenance planning and project tracking. Independent vendor, own domain, no parent branding. IMPORTANT — I checked a name collision before accepting, because the description 'Infrastructure management software platform' is generic enough to fit two unrelated firms. There is a second, entirely different Infrahub: OpsMill's open-source network-infrastructure data platform at opsmill.com / docs.infrahub.app / github.com/opsmill/infrahub. That one is network automation sold to enterprises and telcos. The one at infrahub.ai is road and pavement infrastructure sold to SLED buyers — corroborated by a January 2026 Hart County, Georgia commission vote to pursue a pavement-management assessment and one-year web application pilot with InfraHub, and by DOT usage. For a state and local government job board the road-infrastructure company is the correct matc

paragraphs: InfraHub sells road management software, with a pavement survey that applies ASTM D6433 standards to identify distresses and calculate Pavement Condition Index from 0-100. Asset inventories cover roadside asset mapping and condition assessment, with 20+ asset types available, from stop signs to guardrails, sidewalks, and bike lanes. The road management platform provides tools for end-to-end management of maintenance workflows, including planning and job creation tools and a work management system for tracking project progress.

Data collection uses 360-degree cameras that gather image, GPS, and telemetry data along a road network. Images are processed by AI models that create inventories by identifying and assessing pavement distresses and road assets. Data from the cloud is surfaced in a web application where users can view, edit, and manage their road network. Generated data can be exported in formats including shapefiles and Excel files, and imported into any GIS software.

The pages name State DOTs, City and County DOTs, Municipal DOTs, DPWs, and MPOs, Civil Engineering Firms, and Regional TPOs as the groups served. Pricing is based on a per-mile rate tailored to the set of assets and distresses a customer needs identified. A 1,000-mile road network is typically processed within one month.

paragraphs: Decision Optimization Technology sells asset management and capital planning software for organizations maintaining aging infrastructure. It provides data management and life-cycle cost optimization across all asset classes.

Instead of prioritization alone, it applies years of doctorate-level research on optimization algorithms to build customized multiyear, multi-constraint capital plans. Users collect and maintain inventory data, condition data, and historical repairs across asset types. Map-centric visualizations display condition and other performance indicators by asset type. Risk-based analysis develops models of asset criticality and likelihood of failure. An unlimited number of scenarios can be set to investigate budgeting strategies, policy decisions, and treatment options. Deterioration models are customizable across asset classes. The product runs as a fully web-based application.

Reports come out presentation ready. The company cites a survey by Infrastructure Solutions Inc. of 100 government clients finding that planning decisions are heavily influenced by socio-economic factors. The site notes that Hanson Professional Services Inc. recommends licensing the software. It also discloses that Hanson owns a significant interest in the licensing entity.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "provides government agencies and engineering firms with a unique integrated solution for roadway and infrastructure management" Fetched https://roadman.tech. Live and fully operational - working navigation, login portals, demo booking forms, blog and detailed product pages; not parked, not for sale, no redirect to another company. The quoted line names the company's business in the description's own terms ('roadway and infrastructure management'), and the site further claims 'the only real-time solution for pavement performance analytics'. The stated buyer, 'government agencies and engineering firms', is a direct state and local fit - roadway and pavement management is a city, county and state DOT function. Short domain does not resemble the full name, but 'roadman.tech' is a plain contraction of Roadway Management Technologies and the site self-identifies under the full name. Standalone company, no parent-domain issue.

paragraphs: Roadway Management Technologies provides government agencies and engineering firms with an integrated solution for roadway and infrastructure management. The pavement analytics product uses proprietary sensors mounted on an agency's vehicles, which collect road quality data while those vehicles are driven in daily routine. Hardware is mounted underneath city-owned or county-owned vehicles rather than on a survey vehicle sent out for the purpose. Stretches of road are then compared and ranked by quality, and color-coded on the web-based platform.

Alongside the surveying functionality, the company sells a work order management and record-keeping system integrated with the online map. Work orders can be created for tasks such as pothole repairs, ditch cleanouts, and sign repairs. Crews record maintenance information, photos, and related expenditures on the platform from any internet-connected device. A fleet management service covers driver safety and activity reporting along with vehicle preventative maintenance notifications.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "Fleet Management & Real-Time Fleet Tracking Camera System by EYERIDE" Fetched https://eyeride.io. The page self-identifies as EYERIDE and the H1/title reads 'Fleet Management & Real-Time Fleet Tracking Camera System by EYERIDE'. It ties directly to the description on both halves: fleet video telematics ('Cloud-Based Command Center for Your Vehicles'; 'Live, High Quality Camera System with Included Fast Wi-Fi'; named products EYENVS and 'EYERIDE AI Dash Cam') and driver monitoring ('Driver Behavior and Fleet Safety', with alerts 'whenever they get sleepy, drift from a lane, or need to brake'). Own primary domain, no redirect, not a parent or aggregator. No concerns.

paragraphs: EYERIDE sells a fleet management system that pulls vehicle and driver data into one place for the organizations that run vehicles. The company pitches the result as an IoT solution for any industry.

Cameras anchor the system, with live views and the ability to go back months to retrieve recorded footage. Driver assistance features track following distance, lane departure and the distance to other vehicles, pedestrians or objects. A driver-facing camera reads behavior in the cab, including fatigue, smoking, phone use and an unfastened seatbelt. Warnings for harsh braking, harsh cornering, speeding and traffic violations reach both the cab and the office. Geofencing lets a manager draw areas and get alerts whenever a vehicle enters or leaves one.

For hours-of-service compliance there is a logging app kept to a handful of sections. In-vehicle cellular routers add connectivity, and the 5G model is offered with SASE options including zero trust security. Operators carrying passengers can add a counter that records how many people enter and exit at any given moment. One described use is school transport, where the tools can let educators and parents know the vehicle location. The site claims thousands of users of the platform for fleet operations.

paragraphs: TeamLinkt sells sports registration, scheduling, and administration software to the organizations that run seasons. Registration forms are built inside the platform and payments are collected online, and schedules are published from the same place. An app puts schedules, scores, standings, and updates in front of athletes and their families, with team chat in place of scattered texts and email chains.

League operators get tools for building balanced schedules, tracking standings, assigning officials, and running game day operations across divisions. Clubs and associations get registration templates, rostering, scheduling across fields, courts, and ice times, and tracking of waivers, background checks, and certifications. Governing bodies register and manage their member clubs and associations, track compliance across them, and can run their own competitions.

Core features are free, with a paid bundle for organizations that want more advanced tools. An account is offered with no contract and no credit card. Support is offered over live chat rather than a ticket based queue.

paragraphs: SwimTopia sells web-based swim team management software covering credit card registration, calendar and signups, a custom website, online registration and store, and volunteer management. paragraphs: SportsEngine sells technology for youth sports organizations. Products are grouped into clubs, teams, and leagues, class-based businesses and swimming, livestreaming and a program directory, tournaments and brackets, and volleyball events. Two of those product lines carry former names, GoMotion and TeamUnify for class-based businesses and Tourney Machine for tournaments.

For clubs and associations, the platform collects athlete information, waivers, and payments, runs custom reports on club finances, and confirms coach credentials. It also builds team rosters and schedules, delivers uniforms and team gear, and connects families through a club website and a mobile app. For clubs the platform also covers background checks on coaches and volunteers, athlete safety training, live streaming, fundraising with spirit wear and apparel, team sponsorships, and membership programs.

SportsEngine Motion is aimed at owners of class-based gyms and studios. That product handles class and lesson schedules, invoicing, registration, member messaging, and a website, with private lessons and bookings among the features.

before.name: GameChanger
before.description: Youth sports scorekeeping and streaming app - exhibited at NRPA 2026

paragraphs: GameChanger sells a youth sports app that athletes, coaches, and families use to stay connected through live streaming, scorekeeping, team management, and developmental resources. The app is free for coaches on teams where they are listed as staff.

Coaches message the team, schedule events and lineups, and review stats, insights, and game film for practice planning and player development. Families and fans follow along with real-time live streaming in HD, GameStream animations, live game alerts, and play-by-plays. Confirmed family members and players can broadcast games live in all sports by default. Watching live streams of sports such as basketball, volleyball, and soccer is free without limit.

The company was founded in 2009, is headquartered in New York City, and says it covers more than nine million games annually across baseball, softball, basketball, volleyball, soccer, football, lacrosse, hockey, and more. It also puts its reach at close to 10 million games and more than a million teams a year. GameChanger is owned and operated by DICK'S Sporting Goods, described as one of the largest sporting goods retailers in the United States.

before.name: Upper Hand
before.description: Youth sports program, camp and league management software

paragraphs: Upper Hand sells sports business management software that covers scheduling, registration, payment processing, team management, marketing, and payroll in one place. Programs can be built as private lessons, classes, teams, and clinics, with registration options, capacity controls, and waitlists. Billing covers payments, memberships, pricing plans, discounts, and recurring billing. Staff and facility tools handle instructors, access levels, payroll reporting, and facility availability.

The pages describe the market as sports facilities, academies, and coaching businesses of all sizes. The company page states that Upper Hand serves the sports training industry and helps facilities, academies, and trainers grow their businesses. Customer stories name businesses such as EYG Basketball, SpeedSkills Hockey, and D-BAT Newark.

The company page dates the business to 2012, when a baseball coach started a platform connecting athletes with private coaches. The name Upper Hand dates from 2015, when the team rebranded and described the product as a sports training management platform. A mobile app is available to both the sports business and its clients.

quote.text: Upper Hand was created by sports coaches to make sports training easier.

provenance.quote: From scheduling and registration to payment processing, team management, marketing, payroll, and more, Upper Hand gives you all the tools you need to manage every aspect of your sports business.
Run private lessons, classes, teams, and clinics with flexible registration, capacity controls, and built-in waitlists all in one place.
Accept payments, offer memberships and pricing plans, apply discounts, and automate recurring billing without extra tools.
Manage instructors, access levels, payroll reporting, and facility availability to avoid conflicts and double bookings.
Sports facilities, academies, and coaching businesses of all sizes can benefit from Upper Hand’s comprehensive sports business management software.
Upper Hand serves the sports training industry, helping facilities, academies, and trainers grow their businesses.
With Upper Hand, EYG Basketball has grown their athlete base to 2,500 and saved over 10 hours per week on administrative tasks.
In 2012, baseball coach Kevin MacCauley saw the need for a platform connecting athletes with private coaches.
In 2015, the team rebranded as Upper Hand, the first sports training management platform.
The Upper Hand mobile app is free to download for both the sports business and its clients.

before.name: Byga
before.description: Club and league management platform for youth soccer organizations

paragraphs: Byga makes software for running youth sports organizations. It is built for club leadership, coaches, and families rather than one of the three. The workflows follow a club from preseason through postseason.

Tryouts replace check-in lines, paper evaluations, and missed follow-up emails, then move players into registration. Registration offers flexible pricing, scholarships, and installments. Scheduling plans practices for unlimited teams, syncs league and tournament events, and publishes updates to team calendars. Field allocation runs on drag and drop, with usage controlled through requests and approvals. Club leaders get financial reporting and analytics, player profiles, targeted email campaigns, and real-time chat.

A native iOS and Android app lets team managers and coaches build lineups, perform health checks, check attendance, and upload photos. The company says the product was shaped in collaboration with youth sports clubs across the nation. It points to dedicated onboarding and responsive support for its partner clubs.

paragraphs: This company sells AI-driven youth sports management software marketed as OTTO SPORT AI. It is shaped around feedback from club directors, coaches, families and athletes.

The platform covers club and league management, tournaments, ticketing and athlete recruitment. Tournament and ticketing tools handle registration, scheduling and communication for events. An assistant called OTTO PILOT is meant to help club admins respond to the common questions parents ask every season. A recruiting product, University Athlete, helps athletes find the right colleges to play for and helps college coaches identify athletes to recruit.

The about page describes a lab that exists to harness the power of AI in ways that support club leaders, coaches and families. A group of industry operators helps guide product, customer success and partnerships. The brand is fronted by a mascot named Otto.

paragraphs: Active Network sells activity management software to communities and organizers. Its markets span camps, classes, education, endurance events and parks. The company frames this as scalable management solutions for organizations and municipalities around the world.

Email and SMS tools let an organization or municipality get the word out about what it offers. Reporting and analytics are customizable. The company says its business is routinely and independently assessed for compliance to various security standards. A custom organization app powered by ACTIVENet or Camp & Class Manager gives access to core functionality at any hour.

The company states that it operates across 103 countries. Its history page records that ACTIVE Network was acquired by Vista Equity Partners. The same page notes the opening of its Dallas headquarters. Earlier entries list the acquisition of ReserveAmerica and a strategic alliance agreement with DigitalTown.

brands.name: NextRec (formerly PerfectMind)
brands.description:
PerfectMind is the former name of the product now sold as nextRec, and nextrec.com keeps a page for it that opens "PerfectMind Software is now nextRec". That page defines the product as "a frictionless, all-in-one recreation management software designed for government agencies and private recreation facilities", and says PerfectMind "serves parks and recreation organizations, martial arts studios, higher-education recreation centers, swim schools, homeowner associations, and facilities offering classes and camps to their community members". The government function is the registration-and-facilities back office of a parks and recreation department: online and on-site registration for "courses, private lessons, drop ins", an "intelligent conflict manager" for scheduling community events, one-time and recurring facility rentals with customizable contract templates and digital customer signatures, point of sale for memberships and passes, built-in email marketing so departments do not sync to outside software, and real-time reporting across "any object or table in your database". A Citywide POS module is offered to consolidate payments across a municipality. The brand still has live surfaces: the knowledge base and user community on nextrec.com both sit at community.perfectmind.com, and the PCI DSS certificate the site links to is filed as "PerfectMind PCI DSS Certificate".

The page gives the family history plainly. "PerfectMind was founded in 1998." "PerfectMind's software was acquired by Xplor Technologies in 2020. In 2022, PerfectMind rebranded to become nextRec." On what changed: "The PerfectMind software platform remains built and powered by the same team - aside from changing its name to nextRec the only change is that PerfectMind software is now part of a global ecosystem with powerful backing, integrations, and support." That answers the "why does this one exist" question differently from its siblings: PerfectMind is not a separate product sitting beside nextRec, it is the same product under its previous name, kept addressable because agencies bought it under that name. The same page says "Xplor Technologies is the parent company of PerfectMind" and that Xplor "serves over 140 markets globally, 75,000 customers daily, and employs over 2,000 Xplorers across the globe". One conflict is worth recording rather than resolving: nextrec.com says PerfectMind was founded in 1998, while Xplor's corporate site says "Founded in 1988, NextRec". Both are the family's own materials and they disagree; neither was treated as settled here.

brands.name: ePACT
brands.description:
ePACT Network sells emergency and health forms automation, described on its homepage as "Emergency and health forms automation that integrates seamlessly with rec management systems" and on its parks and recreation page as a way for "rec leaders to collect, manage and access health & emergency information, waivers and consent forms - all in one secure, compliant platform". The government function is narrow and specific: it is the participant-paperwork layer under a parks and recreation department's programs. The site lists what it collects - "emergency forms with contact information and instructions, medical forms, waivers, consent forms, and personal health and safety needs", plus immunization records, medication authorization forms, allergies, dietary restrictions, medical history and signed consent forms. Named capabilities are configurable eForms, online and offline access, multi-channel communications, search, filtering and reporting, API integration, and paperless check-in and check-out with a "tailorable contact pick up list" for who may collect a child. Buyers named on the site are parks and recreation departments, YMCAs, camps and JCCs, schools, and sports associations. Public-sector customers quoted by name include the City of Kettering, OH, the San Francisco Recreation & Park Department, CA, the City of Newton Parks & Recreation, MA, the Town of Cary, NC, and the Deerfield Park District, IL. On compliance the site claims SOC II Type 2, HIPAA in the US, and PIPA, PIPEDA and FOIPPA in Canada, hosted on Microsoft Azure. Families use it free, storing a "Private Personal Emergency Record (PPER)".

ePACT sits differently in the family from the other brands: it is not a system of record for registration, it is the forms layer that attaches to one. Its own site says it integrates "with your existing registration system, like ActiveNet, Daxko, RecTrac (and more!)" - RecTrac being the sibling Vermont Systems product, ActiveNet and Daxko being competitors of the family. That is the answer to why it exists alongside three registration platforms: it is sold across all of them, including rivals. Its distribution runs through associations rather than the Xplor brand - it is "Exclusive Partner of the NRPA" with member discounts, a "Preferred vendor of the YMCA of the USA", and an "Emergency-supplies partner with the Canadian Red Cross". The family tie is real but quiet: the site footer reads "2026 ePACT Network | All Rights Reserved", with no Xplor copyright, yet it carries an Xplor Recreation logo image linking to cehrecreation.com, and ePACT is not one of the four brands listed on Xplor's own Xplor Recreation page. Its origin is on its about page: ePACT was inspired by a friend, Ayumi, separated from her two daughters during the 2011 earthquake and tsunami in Japan, and unable to learn they were safe for a full day.

brands.name: RecDesk
brands.description:
recdesk.com could not be read. Both the apex and www forms answer a plain fetch with an HTTP 202 and a Sucuri interstitial, and a real browser is served a "Robot Challenge Screen" that did not clear on repeated attempts. No attempt was made to defeat it, so nothing below comes from RecDesk's own site. What follows is from Xplor's corporate site, which is the family's own material. Xplor writes: "Founded in 2005, RecDesk provides scalable, easy-to-use software for parks and recreation departments, aquatic centers, schools, community centers, HOAs, and small municipalities. Its integrations with access control, GIS/address databases, and financial systems help teams streamline facility scheduling, program management, and operational workflows - reducing manual effort and system fragmentation." Xplor adds that "Business and community leaders can run more efficient programs, offer better resident experiences, and make data-driven decisions that strengthen their community services."

RecDesk is one of the four brands Xplor lists on its Xplor Recreation page, alongside Vermont Systems, NextRec and CampBrain, and Xplor's "Visit RecDesk" link points to recdesk.com. The distinction Xplor's own wording draws between the siblings is the size and type of buyer: RecDesk is described for "small municipalities", aquatic centers and HOAs, where Vermont Systems is described for "municipal, county, state, and federal military recreation organizations". RecDesk's postings run through the Rippling board shared across this family, clubessential-holdings-cjb, which also carries an asset named Xplor_Logo_withTag_Color.png. Beyond that, this record is deliberately short. Anything further about RecDesk's product, customers or scale would have to be invented, because its site refused to be read.

brands.name: NextRec (formerly PerfectMind)
brands.description:
PerfectMind is the former name of the product now sold as nextRec, and nextrec.com keeps a page for it that opens "PerfectMind Software is now nextRec". That page defines the product as "a frictionless, all-in-one recreation management software designed for government agencies and private recreation facilities", and says PerfectMind "serves parks and recreation organizations, martial arts studios, higher-education recreation centers, swim schools, homeowner associations, and facilities offering classes and camps to their community members". The government function is the registration-and-facilities back office of a parks and recreation department: online and on-site registration for "courses, private lessons, drop ins", an "intelligent conflict manager" for scheduling community events, one-time and recurring facility rentals with customizable contract templates and digital customer signatures, point of sale for memberships and passes, built-in email marketing so departments do not sync to outside software, and real-time reporting across "any object or table in your database". A Citywide POS module is offered to consolidate payments across a municipality. The brand still has live surfaces: the knowledge base and user community on nextrec.com both sit at community.perfectmind.com, and the PCI DSS certificate the site links to is filed as "PerfectMind PCI DSS Certificate".

The page gives the family history plainly. "PerfectMind was founded in 1998." "PerfectMind's software was acquired by Xplor Technologies in 2020. In 2022, PerfectMind rebranded to become nextRec." On what changed: "The PerfectMind software platform remains built and powered by the same team - aside from changing its name to nextRec the only change is that PerfectMind software is now part of a global ecosystem with powerful backing, integrations, and support." That answers the "why does this one exist" question differently from its siblings: PerfectMind is not a separate product sitting beside nextRec, it is the same product under its previous name, kept addressable because agencies bought it under that name. The same page says "Xplor Technologies is the parent company of PerfectMind" and that Xplor "serves over 140 markets globally, 75,000 customers daily, and employs over 2,000 Xplorers across the globe". One conflict is worth recording rather than resolving: nextrec.com says PerfectMind was founded in 1998, while Xplor's corporate site says "Founded in 1988, NextRec". Both are the family's own materials and they disagree; neither was treated as settled here.

brands.name: ePACT
brands.description:
ePACT Network sells emergency and health forms automation, described on its homepage as "Emergency and health forms automation that integrates seamlessly with rec management systems" and on its parks and recreation page as a way for "rec leaders to collect, manage and access health & emergency information, waivers and consent forms - all in one secure, compliant platform". The government function is narrow and specific: it is the participant-paperwork layer under a parks and recreation department's programs. The site lists what it collects - "emergency forms with contact information and instructions, medical forms, waivers, consent forms, and personal health and safety needs", plus immunization records, medication authorization forms, allergies, dietary restrictions, medical history and signed consent forms. Named capabilities are configurable eForms, online and offline access, multi-channel communications, search, filtering and reporting, API integration, and paperless check-in and check-out with a "tailorable contact pick up list" for who may collect a child. Buyers named on the site are parks and recreation departments, YMCAs, camps and JCCs, schools, and sports associations. Public-sector customers quoted by name include the City of Kettering, OH, the San Francisco Recreation & Park Department, CA, the City of Newton Parks & Recreation, MA, the Town of Cary, NC, and the Deerfield Park District, IL. On compliance the site claims SOC II Type 2, HIPAA in the US, and PIPA, PIPEDA and FOIPPA in Canada, hosted on Microsoft Azure. Families use it free, storing a "Private Personal Emergency Record (PPER)".

ePACT sits differently in the family from the other brands: it is not a system of record for registration, it is the forms layer that attaches to one. Its own site says it integrates "with your existing registration system, like ActiveNet, Daxko, RecTrac (and more!)" - RecTrac being the sibling Vermont Systems product, ActiveNet and Daxko being competitors of the family. That is the answer to why it exists alongside three registration platforms: it is sold across all of them, including rivals. Its distribution runs through associations rather than the Xplor brand - it is "Exclusive Partner of the NRPA" with member discounts, a "Preferred vendor of the YMCA of the USA", and an "Emergency-supplies partner with the Canadian Red Cross". The family tie is real but quiet: the site footer reads "2026 ePACT Network | All Rights Reserved", with no Xplor copyright, yet it carries an Xplor Recreation logo image linking to cehrecreation.com, and ePACT is not one of the four brands listed on Xplor's own Xplor Recreation page. Its origin is on its about page: ePACT was inspired by a friend, Ayumi, separated from her two daughters during the 2011 earthquake and tsunami in Japan, and unable to learn they were safe for a full day.

brands.name: RecDesk
brands.description:
recdesk.com could not be read. Both the apex and www forms answer a plain fetch with an HTTP 202 and a Sucuri interstitial, and a real browser is served a "Robot Challenge Screen" that did not clear on repeated attempts. No attempt was made to defeat it, so nothing below comes from RecDesk's own site. What follows is from Xplor's corporate site, which is the family's own material. Xplor writes: "Founded in 2005, RecDesk provides scalable, easy-to-use software for parks and recreation departments, aquatic centers, schools, community centers, HOAs, and small municipalities. Its integrations with access control, GIS/address databases, and financial systems help teams streamline facility scheduling, program management, and operational workflows - reducing manual effort and system fragmentation." Xplor adds that "Business and community leaders can run more efficient programs, offer better resident experiences, and make data-driven decisions that strengthen their community services."

RecDesk is one of the four brands Xplor lists on its Xplor Recreation page, alongside Vermont Systems, NextRec and CampBrain, and Xplor's "Visit RecDesk" link points to recdesk.com. The distinction Xplor's own wording draws between the siblings is the size and type of buyer: RecDesk is described for "small municipalities", aquatic centers and HOAs, where Vermont Systems is described for "municipal, county, state, and federal military recreation organizations". RecDesk's postings run through the Rippling board shared across this family, clubessential-holdings-cjb, which also carries an asset named Xplor_Logo_withTag_Color.png. Beyond that, this record is deliberately short. Anything further about RecDesk's product, customers or scale would have to be invented, because its site refused to be read.

paragraphs: nextRec sells cloud based software for running parks and recreation departments, from program registration to facility rentals, with a self service side for residents. Buyers range from small villages to large counties and the government staff in between.

Staff set up single or recurring classes, courses, drop-ins, and programs, with conflict checking built in. The booking side covers indoor and outdoor facilities, parks, fields, campgrounds, meeting spaces, and party venues. Payments, memberships, and product sales run through the same system, online or on-site. Reports can be created, run, and exported in real time.

The same platform is marketed to K-12 schools and to higher education institutions. Associations use it so members can pay and manage their own accounts at any hour. The company says the platform complies with PCI, ISO, and SOC standards. Customers keep ownership of their data, which the site says stays in its country of origin. Support is offered 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

paragraphs: CommunityPass is cloud-based software that powers schools, recreation centers, community organizations, and sports leagues. It comes from Capturepoint, whose founder the company names as Joe Oriente.

The product began in 2002 with a town Sports Council overwhelmed by hundreds of paper registration forms as athletic sign-ups climbed. The answer was a single account on one website through which families reach registration for every participating organization in town. Departments can offer registration for classes, activities, programs, and trips, with options to buy merchandise and tickets. Payments accept multiple forms with recurring billing and plans while maintaining PCI compliance.

Check-in and check-out are contactless and digital, with pick-up timestamps and real-time emergency contact information for authorized parents. Staff can choose from 300+ pre-built reports covering attendance, financial, roster, and statistical data, or build their own. The company says CommunityPass has grown to serve parks and recreation organizations and schools all across the country.

before.name: Key Data Dashboard
before.description: Lodging occupancy and vacation-rental benchmarking data for DMOs

paragraphs: Key Data sells lodging market data and analytics used by vacation rental property managers, destination organizations, investors and enterprise analytics teams. The argument it makes is that its figures come from actual bookings rather than estimates read off public listing calendars.

The dataset joins direct-source short-term rental reservation data with Airbnb and Vrbo listing coverage and hotel performance benchmarks. The company states integrations with more than 80 property management systems and direct-source data from more than 17,000 property managers, covering over 1.15 million vacation rental properties. Reporting covers occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, guest nights, booking pace and length of stay.

Destination organizations use it to understand event performance, find high-value feeder markets, time campaigns and report results to boards, elected officials and stakeholders. The company says more than 300 destination organizations choose it. Enterprise teams can take the same data through APIs, flat files, S3 buckets, Snowflake delivery or custom feeds rather than through a dashboard.

before.name: Cuseum
before.description: Digital membership, guides and engagement for public museums and cultural sites

paragraphs: Cuseum sells an engagement platform built for museums, cultural attractions, nonprofits and membership organizations. Its digital tools are aimed at the visitors, members and donors those organizations already deal with.

The anchor product is a digital membership card that gives members wallet passes, benefits, renewals and updates through Apple Wallet and Google Wallet. Around it sit mobile engagement, audio guides, ticketing, loyalty tools, donor engagement and lifecycle communication. On site, the platform covers digital tickets, guest registration and barcode scanning at the door. For staff, Cuseum lists native CRM connectors along with 700 or more apps reachable through Zapier.

Cuseum says hundreds of institutions worldwide rely on it for membership cards, mobile guides, guest passes, loyalty programs and lifecycle communications. The customers it describes are kinds of organizations rather than named ones: art museums, science centers, aquariums and zoos, botanical gardens, libraries, alumni associations and nonprofit foundations. The footer identifies the company as Cuseum, Inc., in Boston.

before.name: Bandwango
before.description: Digital destination passes and experience bundles for DMOs and cities

paragraphs: Bandwango sells mobile passes that let a destination showcase its local restaurants, breweries and attractions while tracking visitor interactions. The pitch to tourism organizations is an easier way to measure economic impact.

Staff start from one of the pass templates and customize it to their needs and brand. They then add local places to go, discounts and admissions, with Bandwango helping onboard each business added. Passes work via any browser and save to a phone home screen, so passholders do not download extra apps. Arrival at a location is verified by GPS and merchant verified check-in. Organizations can add rewards to a pass and set a point goal for each one. The product is described as fully white labeled, down to fonts, colors, imagery and logos.

The home page claims over 500 clients. It also claims more than 40,000 local businesses. Paid passes can be featured and resold through a third party network of resellers and distributors. The company says it is an approved connectivity partner, so its passes can appear directly in search results.

before.name: Brandkit
before.description: Digital asset management and media libraries for DMOs and tourism boards

paragraphs: Brandkit gives an organization one searchable, shareable home for its logos, guidelines, images, video, presentations, stories and press releases. It bundles a brand portal, media center, brand guidelines, digital asset management, a CMS, a knowledge library and file transfer into one system. The buyers it names include national and local government agencies, tourism boards, place brands, economic development agencies, universities and franchises.

Uploaded assets are organized with automatic tagging and metadata generated by AI. Search combines multi-faceted keywords with AI-powered semantic search. Brand guidelines, rights management and licensing information surface alongside the assets themselves. The platform also generates llms.txt and llms.html plain text files so chatbots and language models can read the content. Pricing is based on usage rather than per seat, which the company ties to public sector bodies sharing resources with many end users.

The founder writes that Brandkit began in 1994 to fix the same problem it addresses now. The company says it is still privately held, has never taken outside money, and is profitable. It says it runs brand hubs, media centres, image libraries and partner toolkits for tourism boards, place brands, universities and government departments. One published case study covers how VisitScotland built a media library across several organisations.

before.name: CrowdRiff
before.description: Visual content and UGC management for destination marketing organizations

paragraphs: CrowdRiff sells visual content software to travel brands, with the stated aim of giving them content and insights that inspire travelers. The pitch is to plan, produce and measure content in one place, replacing multiple tools with one connected solution.

The platform collects user-generated content from a destination, with curation and rights approval before anything is published. It also sources original short-form video to fuel Instagram Reels, TikToks and YouTube Shorts. Visuals are centralized so a team can search, organize and share content instead of digging through folders and drives.

The site states that more than 900 destinations use CrowdRiff for their visual content. Customer stories cover destination marketing organizations, including one on how Destination Madison plans and produces content. The founders describe starting the company with the vision of a local-first travel ecosystem. It also partners with agencies around the world to help their clients use user-generated content and owned visuals.

before.name: STQRY
before.description: Visitor apps, tours and guides for museums, parks and tourism agencies

paragraphs: STQRY, formerly OnCell, is a storytelling platform used to create location-based tours, virtual tours, mobile and web apps, audio guides, games, and online collections. Images, audio, text and map information are added to a mobile guide app through a web-based tour builder. Tours built in STQRY Apps can be tested and published for mobile web, iOS and Android. Content in a published tour or audio guide can be changed later through the STQRY builder, with updates pushed to the app in real time.

STQRY Kiosk is a separate platform for creating digital labels and interactive storytelling elements for visitors. Kiosk content is offered in 30 different languages, including Arabic, Hebrew, Māori and Papiamento.

The about page dates the business to OnCell's inception in 2006 and describes the destinations served as museums, parks, cities, and historic sites. The apps pricing section states that a setup fee of USD 1,995 applies for native apps.

quote.text: The simple to use app builder for interactive visitor experiences.

provenance.quote: STQRY (formerly OnCell) is a storytelling platform that helps visitors explore further, engage deeper, and discover more. You can choose from a range of amazing features to create location-based tours, virtual tours, mobile, and web apps, audio guides, games, and online collections.
Add images, audio, text, map info and custom features to your mobile guide app with our simple web-based tour builder.
Test and publish your guided tour app with the press of a button, sharing it instantly for mobile web, iOS and Android.
Something new to share? Make changes to your tour or audio guide content through the STQRY builder, and updates will be pushed to your app in real time.

Sharing your curation team’s deep knowledge and engaging insights adds a whole new dimension to your visitor experience. With the simple to use STQRY Kiosk platform, you can create digital labels and richly interactive storytelling elements for your visitors.
STQRY Kiosk offers 30 different languages including RTL languages such as Arabic and Hebrew and indigenous languages like Māori and Papiamento.
Since OnCell's inception in 2006, we have helped thousands of destinations around the world ranging from museums, parks, cities, and historic sites of all sizes to connect with their visitors.
A setup fee of USD 1,995 applies for native apps.

before.name: IDSS
before.description: Cloud CRM and destination sales system for CVBs and tourism bureaus

paragraphs: IDSS sells a cloud-based CRM for the travel and tourism industry. The company says more than 170 destinations around the world run their organizations on the product, called iDSS Cyclone.

It is described as the first web-based CRM platform in the destination marketing sector, with a single codebase that lets new features reach every user each month. Additional software service options and technical support are offered under the Tempest name. The footer lists a phone number alongside a tempest.im address.

before.name: Playground Guardian
before.description: Playground safety inspections plus Park Protector inspection/asset software for munis and schools - exhibited at NRPA 2026

paragraphs: Playground Guardian sells onsite safety inspection of playground equipment and surfacing, checking that they meet safety standards. The company also sells Park Protector, a playground inspection and asset management application that runs on a computer or mobile device. Playground Guardian is based in Charlotte, North Carolina.

Park Protector records inspections on any device with or without cell service, and is built to CPSC Publication 325 and ASTM standards. The surface testing module captures the data fields required by ASTM F1292 and F3313, including HIC, Gmax, impact velocity, and drop height. Inspections, surface tests, issues, work orders, and complaints export to PDF or Excel.

Park Protector is offered for managing inspections across city-owned play spaces and facilities. The software page names parks, school districts, and municipal facilities across the United States. Park Protector is presented for organizations ranging from solo CPSI inspectors to large municipal departments. Organizations that already have maintenance staff managing their facilities are offered the Park Protector app.

quote.text: Park Protector replaces clipboards, spreadsheets, and disconnected tools with a single app built around how inspection professionals actually work: in the field, across dozens of locations, with or without a signal.

provenance.quote: Get a thorough assessment of playground equipment, surfacing, and more to ensure they meet safety standards.

Park Protector is an easy-to-use playground inspection and asset management application. Manage, monitor, and inspect any municipal, neighborhood, or school playground system from your computer or mobile device.
Playground Guardian is a 3rd-generation American company based in Charlotte, North Carolina.

before.name: Novo Solutions
before.description: Work order and park maintenance management software for municipalities

paragraphs: Novo Solutions sells an operations management system called NovoGov, described on its site as a web and mobile cloud-based software solution for streamlining operations. The homepage lists the software as tracking and maintaining assets, receiving and processing work orders and inspections, providing customer support, and reporting on outcomes and progress. Other functions on that page include viewing assets on a map with maintenance history, and mobile or website access for citizens to submit requests and receive notifications.

The about page states that Novo Solutions has provided customer-driven web solutions since 1999, with technology and pricing scaled to a single department or across multiple departments. The same page names ShareNet as a cloud based information management system launched in 2013, with apps for work order management, asset management, and inventory management.

The case studies page describes public works and utilities departments adopting NovoGov for asset tracking, work order history, and citizen complaints. One case study describes a police department that adopted NovoGov to modernize asset and inventory management after a surprise audit revealed gaps in real-time inventory and historical records. Another describes a township road department that gained maps of assets, digital pre-trip inspections, and automated preventive maintenance.

quote.text: The NovoGov Operations Management system is an easy-to-use, highly flexible web and mobile cloud-based software solution designed to help organizations streamline their operations.

provenance.quote: The NovoGov Operations Management system is an easy-to-use, highly flexible web and mobile cloud-based software solution designed to help organizations streamline their operations.
Receive and Process Work Orders & Inspections,
Mobile/website access for citizens to submit requests and receive notifications.
Since 1999 Novo Solutions’ focus has been to provide customer-driven web solutions that are robust and easy to implement and use.
In 2013 we launched ShareNet – a very flexible, easy to use, cloud based information management system.

The City of Rockland, Maine’s Public Works and Transfer Station, led by Public Works Director Todd Philbrook, transitioned to NovoGov for streamlined work order management, fleet operations, and citizen complaints.
The Stafford Township Police Department managed millions of dollars in vehicles, gear, and equipment using spreadsheets and an outdated CAD system, leaving them unprepared for audits.

After implementing NovoGov, the department gained clear GIS-based maps of assets, digital pre-trip inspections, automated preventive maintenance, and a centralized, map-based to-do list for work orders and complaints.

before.name: greehill
before.description: Lidar digital-twin tree inventories and urban forest management for cities (US via Davey partnership)

paragraphs: greehill turns an urban forest into a continuously updated, predictive system that reveals the condition of every tree and anticipates risk early. The company captures street-level tree data, builds verified digital twins, and turns them into operational metrics and predictive signals across streets, parks, and districts. LiDAR scanning, AI analysis, and operational workflows connect in one system for predicting change and managing trees every day.

Cities are the buyer named on these pages, and greehill works with cities across nearly all continents, creating verified, citywide tree inventories. Within those cities the pages name arborists who inspect trees every day, commissioners who approve budgets and answer to the public, and infrastructure teams who need facts. The output is described as more than 70 measurable metrics, from field operations to city-level planning, reporting, and infrastructure investment.

Cities choose how to execute: in-house, with existing partners, or with regional greehill partners, while the system, the data standard, and quality assurance remain with greehill. Cities worldwide use it in daily operations to manage urban infrastructure from capitals to regional districts.

quote.text: What if your city could understand every tree as part of a living system?

before.name: Outdoorlink
before.description: SmartLink IoT remote monitoring and control of lighting, power, and assets for parks and campuses - exhibited at NRPA 2026, Washington Recreation and Park Association 2026
before.source: NRPA 2026; Washington Recreation and Park Association 2026

paragraphs: Outdoorlink sells remote monitoring and control for outdoor electrical systems and displays, managed from one central platform. The homepage names a Smart Controller for remote asset monitoring, Vantage for detecting screen issues on digital ads, and an LED Luminaire sold on reduced energy cost. The listed uses run to lights, locks, signs, water features, Wifi and digital out-of-home displays.

The industries named are Parks & Recreation, Campus, Transit, Commercial Properties, Smart Asset Management, and Digital Place Based. Case studies on the site cover a county parks and recreation department, four transit agencies, three outdoor advertising companies, and a historic landmark. Those studies name Hillsborough County Parks and Recreation Department, Kansas City Area Transportation Authority, Long Beach Transit, Orange County Transportation Authority, Lamar Advertising Company, Stott Outdoor Advertising, and Circle City Outdoor. The homepage puts the count at 1,200+ organizations that rely on Outdoorlink to manage and monitor lighting and assets.

quote.text: Take control of your electrical systems and displays with Outdoorlink. Manage, monitor, and adjust lighting, signs, water features, OOH ads, and more from one central platform in real-time.

provenance.quote: Take control of your electrical systems and displays with Outdoorlink. Manage, monitor, and adjust lighting, signs, water features, OOH ads, and more from one central platform in real-time.

before.description: TreePlotter urban forestry inventory and canopy software for municipalities

acquired.deal: Acquired by Waverock Software (Scottsdale, Arizona) — completed April 2023, announced in a PRWeb release dated 2023-04-17 and in PlanIT Geo's own post 'PlanIT Geo Acquired By Waverock Software. This Is What It Means' (2023-04-21). No acquisitions made by PlanIT Geo found.

paragraphs: PlanIT Geo states that it is a global urban forestry software development and consulting firm, working on urban forestry, parks, and arboriculture since 2012. The products named are the TreePlotter Software Suite together with PlanIT Geo services for urban forestry, parks, and sustainability programs. Tree canopy data is described as subscription-based and driven by artificial intelligence.

The home page names greenspace managers and tree care companies around the world as the people this urban forestry and software provider serves. Separate paths on the same page point to community programs, to businesses seeking more work, and to corporate, university, medical campus, or HOA settings. A news item on the about page quotes a city planning director on an application named TreePlotter CANOPY.

paragraphs: ROLLER sells venue management software to attractions businesses, pulling bookings, point of sale, memberships and reporting into a single platform. It is cloud-based and built for growing attractions businesses, meant to stand in for the several tools a venue would otherwise run. The company describes the platform as powering more than 3,000 attractions.

Ticketing is built around flexible bookings and add-on sales for both staff and guests. Operators running more than one site can hold branding consistent across locations and publish changes from a single headquarters account. One franchise operator, We Rock the Spectrum, put the platform into more than 120 locations over six months. before.name: 24/7 Software
before.description: Incident, event day and operations management for public venues and cities

paragraphs: 24/7 Software sells operations management software that venue teams use to communicate in real time and hold down risk on event day. The buyers run stadiums, arenas, performing arts centers and other event spaces.

Staff build their own workflows, dispatch personnel and keep a detailed history of every incident record. Each record and every change to it is time and date stamped, so a response leaves an audit trail behind it. Field staff work from mobile applications for iOS and Android that let them file incident forms and close issues where they stand. The same platform schedules preventive maintenance through a computerized maintenance management system. Analytics dashboards are offered as a way to take guesswork out of guest experience and operating decisions.

Beyond ticketed sport, the company aims the software at amusement parks, zoos, aquariums, museums and fairs. College athletics departments and university facilities are named too, covering game day and wider campus operations. The company says its customer success group trains staff and supports them through onboarding.

Organizers build maps from scratch or on Google Maps with a drag-and-drop event mapping tool. Booths are assigned and spaces connected to tickets from that same place. paragraphs: Manage My Market sells online software for running farmers markets, described on the site as a solution designed to simplify vendor management for farmers market operators. The company is based in Portland, Oregon. The site dates the work with market managers to 2003, and says the platform began when a market manager teamed up with a developer.

The platform covers vendor application processing, stall assignments, accounting, analytics, interactive maps, and product search. Market managers approve vendors, assign stalls, enter sales and payments, send invoices, track licenses, send emails, and run reports. Accounting records PayPal, Square, and Stripe transactions automatically, and license reporting flags vendors with missing, expired or current licenses.

Vendors create a company profile, upload licenses and other documentation, and apply to markets in their area. The site says farmers markets across all 50 states, as well as in Canada, the UK, and Australia, are supported.

before.name: Bond Sports
before.description: Sports facility and program management for municipal and community facilities

paragraphs: Bond Sports sells the software that a sports facility runs its business on. It aims at operators of complex multi-sport venues and ice rinks rather than youth clubs alone.

Scheduling, registration, memberships and payments sit on one data model, so availability, billing and reporting stay in sync when something moves. Rentals, events and leagues share a single calendar with recurring bookings, conflict checks and invoicing. Point of sale covers terminals, concessions, merchandise and pro shop sales. Failed membership charges and missing cards are flagged and retried automatically.

Facility types listed include aquatics, fitness, dance, youth sports, parks and recreation departments and universities. Named users quoted on the site include the general manager of Chelsea Piers Sky Rink. The company says customers process more than $250M in registrations a year through the platform. Most facilities go live in three to four weeks. Data migration, configuration and staff training are handled by Bond during the switch.

before.name: Athletify
before.description: Staff scheduling software built for parks and rec departments (flat annual pricing) - exhibited at NRPA 2026

paragraphs: Athletify makes staff scheduling software for parks and recreation departments, pulling every program and every worker into one schedule that a manager can filter as needed. Staff need only one login even when they hold several positions.

Shifts can be filtered and grouped by program, location, position, or staff member, and the views a department reaches for most often can be saved. Requests to drop a shift, claim a shift, or take time off arrive in a centralized inbox that all admins share. Age limitation tools let a department create and enforce scheduling rules for younger workers, including restrictions that keep them off early morning or late evening shifts. Messaging is built in, with channels for different staff groups such as lifeguards or referees.

The company says it has heard from hundreds of cities about the struggle of managing staff, and it is looking for beta partners to help shape the tool. Pricing is advertised without tiers or per-user fees. The site dates the beta program as running until July 1, 2025.

acquired.deal: Acquired by Banyan Software on 12 June 2024, terms undisclosed; founder Bob Cote stayed on as CEO. Announced on the acquirer's own site: https://banyansoftware.com/2024/06/12/subitup. SubItUp's own site makes no mention of it.

paragraphs: SubItUp sells workforce scheduling and time-management software for shift-based teams. The platform builds staff schedules, lets employees swap and pick up shifts without manager intervention, tracks hours with a built-in time clock, and exports hours worked straight to payroll. A built-in time clock can turn any internet-enabled device into a clock-in point, and hours reconcile automatically before they reach payroll.

The pages name higher education, municipal parks and recreation, healthcare, retail and franchise, and live events among the settings the software is built for. Staff can add, drop, and swap their own shifts with peers, and a manager approves the swap once staff agree to it. Managers set the maximum hours staff can work by role and location, including across teams within one organization.
Payroll exports are built for platforms including ADP, Intuit QuickBooks, Oracle PeopleSoft, Workday, and Paychex. Pricing is based on the number of employees scheduled, with a 10-employee minimum.

before.name: EZFacility
before.description: Facility, league and program scheduling for rec centers and parks

paragraphs: EZFacility sells online scheduling, management and membership software for gyms, fitness centers, sports facilities and more. Among the business types it names are gyms and health and fitness centers.

Scheduling centralizes physical resources and consolidates classes, clinics and rentals into a color-coded schedule. League and tournament schedules can handle an even or odd number of teams, single byes, or back-to-back double headers. Referee assignments, printable scorecards and photo ID cards for player verification keep games running on time. Staff can be compensated for sessions, classes or clinics completed and for services sold. Payments run through an integrated PCI-compliant product at what the company calls a competitive rate. A branded mobile app gives clients facility information, schedules, trainer profiles and push notifications.

The company says it was created in 2003. It describes itself as one of the largest providers of management software for the sports and fitness industries. It claims thousands of businesses around the world as customers. The software is hosted on Amazon Web Services with a stated 99.99% uptime.

before.name: CourtReserve
before.description: Court booking, membership, and event management for tennis, pickleball, and padel facilities incl. muni complexes

paragraphs: CourtReserve makes software for running racquet and paddle sports clubs. The platform covers bookings, payments, memberships, events and a mobile app. It is built for racquet and paddle sports facilities.

Clubs run everything from court reservations to payments in one system. Invoicing and billing are automated to keep the books tidy. Players find their club, search and book from a phone. The player app is available on iOS and Android. The company advertises US-based support.

In a letter on the site, Tim Owens writes that back in 2016 he and Ashley, driven by a love for tennis and pickleball, set out to change how clubs and facilities are run. The same letter describes a community that ranges from local clubs to organizations such as the USTA, PTR and PPR. Case studies present the software as a way to simplify scheduling, grow membership and manage reservable spaces. One of them says the pickleball operator Dill Dinkers adopted CourtReserve as its club management system from day one.

before.name: Skedda
before.description: Space and facility booking platform used by municipal and campus facilities

paragraphs: Skedda sells booking software for shared workplace space, giving staff self-serve booking of desks, rooms and other resources. The company frames it as one platform to book space and manage operations, backed by data about how the square footage is used.

before.name: Greenzie
before.description: Autonomous mowing software retrofitting commercial mowers, sold via OEMs to grounds and parks crews - exhibited at AB Show 2026

paragraphs: Greenzie makes self-driving software meant to improve the safety, productivity and profitability of a landscaping fleet. It partners with OEMs to manufacture Greenzie-equipped, Robotic Ready mowers sold at outdoor power equipment dealers throughout the United States. Buyers shop for those mowers at dealer locations nationwide.

Each Greenzie-equipped mower carries sensors the company says are field tested for obstacle avoidance, smooth driving and clean stripes. Operators can switch between manual and autonomous modes. A crew mows the perimeter once and lets the software finish the job while they move on to other tasks. The software is designed in accordance with ANSI/RIA R15.08-1-2020 safety requirements for industrial robots.

The customers are commercial landscaping crews, and the company frames its work as making jobs easier, faster and safer for large landscapers across the country. Greenzie began in 2018, when co-founder Charles Brian Quinn started calling every landscaper he could reach. The team describes itself as roboticists, software engineers and landscaping professionals. It says it is backed by venture capital firms and investors.

before.name: HydroPoint Data Systems
before.description: WeatherTRAK smart irrigation and water management for public agencies

paragraphs: HydroPoint sells smart water management covering both indoor and outdoor use. That means round-the-clock water use analytics and leak detection alongside irrigation control. Two irrigation brands sit under the company: WeatherTRAK, for portfolio-wide remote management and visibility, and Baseline, which offers sensors and two-wire technology.

A third product, WaterCompass, provides real-time visibility into indoor water use. The company says its solutions typically deliver payback in as little as 24 to 36 months. It also claims benefits past the water bill, including reduced labor and operational costs and prevention of overwatering.

HydroPoint was founded in 2002 by technology entrepreneurs Chris Spain, Peter Carlson, and Chris Manchuck. In 2016 it expanded by acquiring Baseline Systems. One published case study reports that the City of Boise has seen up to 70% water savings on its Baseline sites compared with previous watering methods. Across its customers, the company reports saving over 27 billion gallons of onsite water and over $213 million in water costs in 2025.

The software carries the names AppManager, BaseManager, BACnet Manager and PipeView Analytics. Project highlights describe how Longwood Cricket Club uses Baseline products to manage its tennis court complex. Another highlight covers Baseline at the 9/11 Memorial. paragraphs: Rain Bird sells irrigation equipment and control systems, and its home page presents commercial projects as a separate demand on those systems. paragraphs: Sterling Volunteers sells volunteer background screening services to nonprofits and volunteer programs across the country. The screening platform is described as tailor-made for volunteer managers, nonprofits and service organizations that want to avoid onboarding risky individuals. Volunteers who are screened and vetted join an online community and can connect with multiple service organizations.

Sectors named on the site include education, where volunteers are screened at colleges and universities, secondary schools, libraries, and research institutions. Healthcare screening covers volunteers working at hospitals, clinics, laboratories, nursing facilities and relief organizations. Sports screening covers youth coaches, referees, and others volunteering with amateur, Olympic and youth sports teams.

Pricing depends on the breadth and depth of the checks, and the cost may be as low as $10 per background check. Two screening packages are offered to clients, an Advanced Package and a Complete Package. The majority of searches are returned in 24 to 72 hours.

paragraphs: Ankored automates safety and compliance work for youth sports programs, from background checks on adults through to verification of the players themselves. The company says it brings youth and adult requirements under federal, state and governing body standards into one system.

One case study on the site describes a parks department replacing paper forms with a digital system covering 26 recreation centers. The company's writing points to more than thirty states that now require background checks.

before.name: Bchex
before.description: Background screening and volunteer management for schools and youth-serving organizations - exhibited at NRPA 2026

paragraphs: Bchex runs background screening for organizations that have to vet the people they hire, and it also sells continuous monitoring along with visitor and volunteer management. The company advertises that 92% of background checks are delivered in under 24 hours.

A customer requests checks in seconds, tracks progress in real time from a single dashboard, and gets a report at the end. Candidates can scan a driver's license so their information populates automatically instead of being typed in. The platform connects to an applicant tracking system to sync and automate the screening process. Bchex puts terms behind the service: no payment if it misses its turnaround time or if the customer is unsatisfied, and a price match against a cheaper quote.

The company counts more than 2,000 school districts, non-profits, and US businesses among its customers. It states that it processes over 500,000 background checks per year. It describes nearly 30 years spent on this one line of work. The site states that Bchex is SOC 2 Type 2 certified for security, confidentiality, and availability. Buyers pay per order, with no long-term contracts or subscription fees.

before.name: Player's Health
before.description: Risk management, insurance and safety compliance for youth sports

paragraphs: Players Health sells insurance together with the staff and software a sports program needs to keep participants protected. The company dates the work to 2016 and has widened the roster since then to insurance, athlete safety, and employee benefits products and services. On the insurance side it describes athlete-first protection sold to youth sports nationwide.

Policies cover a league or program against unexpected accidents, injuries, or property damage. A separate directors and officers line is offered as legal protection for a board. Alongside the policies sits a suite of athlete safety products meant to protect youth and amateur athletes, fitness club members, and student athletes. Programs that do not know where to begin can ask for a Players Health Safety Score to work out what steps they need. Training is pitched at coaches and organizations building team cultures and keeping their programs positive and safe. A reporting platform carries incidents from the first report through to resolution.

The founder, Tyrre, started the company after a playing career at Winona State and in the Canadian Football League was plagued with injuries. By its own account the company now supports over 40,000 sports organizations, impacting more than 5 million athletes. It states its mission as creating the safest and most accessible environments for athletes to play the sports they love.

paragraphs: BarkPass sells software for pet licensing and dog park management, aimed at local governments and at private operators of dog parks. The company describes one system meant to raise revenue, improve safety and connect an agency with its community.

before.name: Campspot

paragraphs: Campspot sells campground management and reservation software to park owners and operators. It also runs a consumer booking site where campers search campgrounds, RV parks, cabins, and glamping stays.

On the operations side the software reaches from the front desk to housekeeping. Dashboards and reports track a park's health metrics. The platform connects to dozens of third-party applications. Software customers can show real-time availability on the consumer site for guests to search, discover, and book. Listing on that marketplace is not sold separately from the software.

Campspot serves more than 3,500 parks across the U.S. and Canada, including private RV parks and campgrounds, public parks, franchises, multi-park groups, and investment groups. The company was founded in 2015 to bring a modern booking experience to the camping industry. The marketplace itself launched in the winter of 2020. Campspot is headquartered in Grand Rapids, Michigan.
